page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-standard-56 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 56 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 28 physical cores with multithreading enabled at 2 threads per core. It features 224 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor configuration includes a 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and a 32 MB L3 cache. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type, and it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core compute capabilities and exceptional memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier status in PassMark memory testing and registers strong performance in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU benchmarks. Cryptographic and mathematical operations are highly efficient, as evidenced by strong scores in PassMark CPU encryption and physics tests, alongside robust Redis SET performance of 61.92 million operations per second. Multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and image processing also perform in the top 25% tier. However, large-block memory bandwidth and single-threaded compression tasks fall within the average range.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c2d-standard-56 offers high resource density for compute-heavy workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures predictable execution times, making it a reliable choice for production environments. This instance is highly suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation pipelines, database operations, and medium-scale language model text generation. It also serves as an effective platform for containerized microservices and general-purpose enterprise workloads requiring a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio.
